o1.biggest_strength: The phased rollout discipline. Tying email waves directly to staged rollout percentages and a sub-10% migration ticket threshold protects our tiny 3-person support team from getting crushed like last year.
o1.biggest_mistake: Ranked the channel table by retention rate rather than total retained users (which would place X second above Authors), though the written logic and focus on Authors/YouTube still holds up.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Explicitly highlight the newcomer persona ('Start with five' / where to start) within the launch-day X post thread or onboarding link.

o2.biggest_strength: Great message positioning for both personas (especially 'Start with five' for PMs/designers) and crisp social copy that explicitly leaves room for measured benchmark numbers.
o2.biggest_mistake: Emailing all 420,000 users on Day 1 while telling them to bypass the staged rollout via 'Check for updates' completely defeats the purpose of staging to protect support capacity.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Align the email blast with the staged rollout waves instead of inviting the entire list to manual-update on day one, and set a realistic migration gate instead of an impossible 'zero lost hotkeys across 1,000 users'.

reason: Output 1 thinks like an operator who actually has to manage the blast radius: it stages the email waves alongside the app rollout so support doesn't drown. Output 2 blasts 420,000 people on day one and tells them how to bypass the staged rollout, which would trigger the exact support crisis we had in 2025.
